response.sql:
WITH status_averages AS (
  SELECT 
    COALESCE(rfistat, 'NO_STATUS') as rfi_status,
    AVG(modindex) as avg_modindex
  FROM signals
  WHERE modindex IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY COALESCE(rfistat, 'NO_STATUS')
),
baseline_calc AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(avg_modindex) as baseline
  FROM status_averages
),
kept_statuses AS (
  SELECT 
    sa.rfi_status,
    sa.avg_modindex,
    bc.baseline
  FROM status_averages sa
  CROSS JOIN baseline_calc bc
  WHERE sa.avg_modindex > bc.baseline
),
kept_stats AS (
  SELECT 
    AVG(avg_modindex) as mean_of_kept
  FROM kept_statuses
)
SELECT 
  ks.rfi_status,
  ks.avg_modindex,
  ks.avg_modindex - ks.baseline as above_baseline,
  ks.avg_modindex - kst.mean_of_kept as diff_from_mean_kept
FROM kept_statuses ks
CROSS JOIN kept_stats kst
ORDER BY ks.rfi_status;

assumptions.assumption: Signals with NULL rfistat are grouped as 'NO_STATUS', a distinct group separate from all non-NULL rfistat values.
Signals with NULL modindex are excluded from average calculations ('ignoring missing values').
'Above the baseline' means strictly greater than (>), not greater-than-or-equal (>=).

alternatives.interpretation: Interpret 'above the baseline' as greater-than-or-equal (>=), including RFI statuses whose average modindex equals the baseline.
